record.original_question: Let A be a purely inseparable form of the polynomial ring k^[n] over a field k, meaning that after extension to the perfect closure K of k the algebra A becomes isomorphic to K^[n]. If A is k-rational, so that its quotient field is isomorphic to k^(n), must A already be trivial? More strongly, must A be trivial whenever it is birationally contained in k^[n]?

artifact.category_tag: Purely inseparable forms of affine space
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let k be a field of positive characteristic p, and let K denote the perfect closure of k. Let k^{[n]} stand for the polynomial ring in n variables over k, and let k^{(n)} stand for the purely transcendental field extension k(x_1, ..., x_n). A k-algebra A is called a purely inseparable k-form of k^{[n]} if A ⊗_k K is isomorphic, as a K-algebra, to K^{[n]}. The form A is said to be trivial if A is isomorphic to k^{[n]} as a k-algebra; A is called k-rational if its field of fractions is k-isomorphic to k^{(n)}; and A is said to be birationally contained in k^{[n]} if there exists a k-algebra embedding of A into k^{[n]} that induces an isomorphism of fraction fields after localization (equivalently, the fraction field of A embeds as a k-subfield of k^{(n)} with the same transcendence degree n).

(a) If A is a purely inseparable k-form of k^{[n]} which is k-rational, must A be trivial?

(b) More strongly, if A is a purely inseparable k-form of k^{[n]} which is birationally contained in k^{[n]}, must A be trivial?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turned up related work on separable and purely inseparable A_n-forms (e.g., Kambayashi's triviality theorem for separable forms and Asanuma's constructions of nontrivial purely inseparable A^1-forms), and surveys on the Zariski Cancellation Problem touch on related territory, but no source was located that definitively settles the k-rational / birationally-contained triviality question for purely inseparable forms of k^{[n]} in general. The current status could not be verified.

status_evidence.title: On separable A^2- and A^3-forms
status_evidence.snippet: Separable A^n-forms are trivial in low dimensions; nontrivial purely inseparable A^1-forms exist (Asanuma).
status_evidence.claim: Background indicates the purely inseparable case is genuinely different and nontrivial forms exist, but does not resolve the k-rational case.

status_evidence.title: The Zariski Cancellation Problem and related problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of cancellation and form problems in affine algebraic geometry.
status_evidence.claim: Recent survey discusses related questions on forms of affine space without indicating a resolution of this particular question.
